blocks.title: Introduction
blocks.content:
Let $(X_n)_{n \in \N}$ be a sequence of real-valued random variables. In the series of papers \cite{JKN11,DKN11,KN10,KN12,FMN13}, we introduced the notion of mod-Gaussian convergence (and more generally of mod-convergence with respect to an infinitely divisible law $\phi$):

\begin{definition}\label{def:mod}
The sequence $(X_n)_{n \in \N}$ is said to converge in the mod-Gaussian sense with parameters $t_n \to +\infty$ and limiting (or residue) function $\theta$ if, locally uniformly in $\R$,
$$\esper[\E^{\I t X_n}]\,\E^{\frac{t_n\,t^2}{2}} = \theta(t) \,(1+o(1)),$$

blocks.title: Mod-Gaussian convergence for the Ising model: the transfer matrix method
blocks.content:
\label{sec:ising}

In this section, $(\sigma(i))_{i \in \lle 1,n\rre}$ is a random configuration of spins under the Ising measure \eqref{eq:isingmeasure}, and $M_n=\sum_{i=1}^n \sigma(i)$ is its magnetization. The mod-Gaussian convergence of $M_n$ after appropriate rescaling can be obtained by two different methods: the \emph{transfer matrix method}, which yields an explicit formula for $\esper[\E^{zM_n}]$; and the \emph{cumulant method}, which gives an explicit combinatorial formula for the coefficients of the power series $\log \esper[\E^{zM_n}]$.
